title: Token framing normalizer and template compatibility gating for model onboarding
creator: Ava Patel
description: When onboarding new model bundles we publish both a pinned model version and a performance profile used for routing and cost estimates. During recent onboards we observed small but material token-count deltas caused by differences in how role markers, whitespace, and subtle unicode separators are tokenized across model variants. These deltas cause two problems: 1) the published performance profile's token-per-turn numbers diverge from real traffic and 2) some chat templates result in misaligned role tokens leading to off-by-one KV cache misuses. This ticket implements a lightweight "token framing normalizer" plus a template compatibility gate so that performance profiles are only published when tokenizer-template agreement passes a set of automated probes.
acceptance_criteria: Token framing normalizer library implemented and added to onboarding pipeline (canonicalizes common role markers, collapse-spaces, and maps a small set of unicode separators to canonical U+2029/space sequences).
Compatibility probe added: run a templated fuzz suite across the model's tokenizer and the canonical templates, producing a token-delta histogram and flagging >3% average delta for investigation.
Performance profile publish step gated: profile artifacts are withheld and a human review checklist is created if compatibility probe fails; successful probes automatically allow profile publish.
E2E regression tests added to CI validating pinned bundles produce matching token counts for the standard chat templates used in production (system, user, assistant).
Benchmark shows <1.5% median token inflation for normalized framing compared to prior baseline for pinned onboards, and no KV-cache misalignment incidents in canary testing (2 weeks).
Documentation and runbook published describing fallback shim behavior and rollback steps for pinned rollouts.

2025-02-12: Spike completed — measured tokenizer deltas across 14 candidate bundles. Observed median 4.2% token delta on system-led templates for one model family when role markers used '

' vs '
System:
'.

2025-02-18: Implemented initial framing-normalizer prototype (JS + Python) that performs: role marker normalization, collapse of repeated whitespace, and unicode separator mapping. Added property-based fuzz harness for templates.

2025-02-22: Benchmarks against runtime-1.18: normalization adds median +0.6 token overhead per conversation but reduces variance; KV-cache miss tracing shows elimination of a class of off-by-one cache misses in bench harness.

2025-02-25: RFC review with PM and Design (Sofia Martinez) — agreed gating threshold 3% average token-delta and escalation path to runbook. Design requested an explicit telemetry tag to surface when normalizer alters role markers.

2025-02-28: Opened PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287 (python normalizer), github.com/redwood-inference/onboard/pull/192 (compat probe integration). CI failing on a flaky tokenizer edge-case (nonbreaking-space handling).

2025-03-04: Fixed NBSP handling and added test cases for bidirectional markers. Began canary pipeline: run compatibility probe + publish to staging-only performance-profile registry on successful runs. Monitoring dashboards created for compatibility probe pass/fail rate (link below).
